text: Authentication verifies a user identity. Multi factor authentication combines a password with a second factor such as a security key.
Authorization determines which resources an authenticated user can access. Role based access control grants permissions through roles.
A cache stores frequently requested results for faster access. Time to live controls when cached entries expire.
A message queue buffers work between producers and consumers. Workers process queued jobs asynchronously and may retry failures.
Database backups preserve recoverable copies of data. Test restoration regularly to confirm the backup can be used.
Database indexes speed up lookups at the cost of extra storage and slower writes. Query plans show whether an index is used.
Rate limiting caps the number of requests a client can send in a time window. It protects an API from overload.
Observability uses logs metrics and traces to explain system behavior. Distributed traces follow a request across services.
A canary deployment sends a small share of traffic to a new release before wider rollout. Rollback restores the previous version.
Encryption protects data in transit with TLS and data at rest with encrypted storage. Key rotation limits exposure from compromised keys.
Retrieval augmented generation finds relevant documents before producing an answer. Citations connect an answer to source passages.
Retrieval evaluation measures recall at k and mean reciprocal rank against labelled source documents. Separate held out questions reduce tuning bias.
